steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Combine ketchup, brown sugar, and Worcestershire sauce in a medium bowl.
Cut bacon strips in half. Wrap one slice of bacon around each chestnut and secure with a toothpick. Arrange water chestnut wraps in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 to 15 minutes. Remove water chestnut wraps from the oven and drain some grease. Pour ketchup sauce over wraps.
Bake until bacon is crispy and sauce thickens, 30 to 35 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon-Wrapped Water Chestnuts
raw_recipe.description: These bacon-wrapped water chestnuts are coated in a sauce of ketchup, brown sugar, and Worcestershire, then baked to perfection for an easy appetizer.
raw_recipe.name: Bacon-Wrapped Water Chestnuts

review.reviewBody: These are awesome. I found the secret of making them super crispy, after reading all the reviews. I put the bacon wrapped waterchestnuts on a wire rack over a 9X 12 baking pan, and baked them until they were crispy...then I put the sauce over...yum. Incredible appetizer.

I found that you can cut the bacon in thirds instead of half. Cutting the sauce recipe in half works too. I marinated the water chestnuts for a 1/2 before wrapping them in the bacon. It gave them more flavor. Then i used the marinade to baste them before cooking. Draining the fat off during cooking time helped alot too.

I made these and followed the directions except I took them out of the fat and pan and transferred them to a new clean pan. The bacon was rubbery and not crispy at all. I would cook them a lot longer and make sure they are crispy before I put the sauce on them next time! The sauce is great!

We LOVE this recipe, but I feel like we've perfected it to both make life easier, and make it extra special. -We use pre-cooked bacon from Costco.... so much easier, and no worries about bacon not crisping up... and it's still malleable. -We cook on a rack like some others have mentioned, and we dip the whole wrapped chesnut in the bowl of sauce for a nice thick coating. -We cook it WAY longer. Cook until it's ALMOST burned, and the sauce turns to candy. We don't re-apply sauce or anything, just leave it to bake. We like the sauce as is. So yummy!

I make these 2-3 times a year by request for parties and Holidays. This recipe is the closest I have found to how I actually make them. I use 1/2 cup brown sugar instead of the full cup, 1 cup of chili sauce and 1 cup of ketchup. I also add a tablespoon or two of soy sauce (in addition to Worcestershire) to taste. Sometimes I add another 1/4 cup of brown sugar if the sauce needs it. I cut the bacon in thirds and cut most of the chestnuts in half to make them more bite sized. 

When I am taking these to a party I pre bake them in the oven without sauce for 10-15 mins. Then I dip each one into the sauce and transfer to a crock pot on low. I pour the remaining sauce over the contents in the pot. This way you can just take the pot to the party and people can dig in. When I make these at home I pre bake them as I said above and then dip and transfer to a 9x13 pan and finish baking in the oven. I have also used maple bacon to wrap the ‘nuts but keep the brown sugar to a minimum of you do that. 

I also heat the sauce in a small saucepan to make sure all of the elements combine. I think it glazes the bits better this way. Seriously the Heinz chili sauce makes the sauce really special- give it a try!

These are truly a rave at parties. I made just a few changes. Like the other reviewers, I used less than half a strip of bacon, because even using "regular cut" bacon, half was very thick and I worried about it cooking all the way through. 

 I added about 1.5 to 2 tsps. of sriracha to the full recipe to give it nice little kick. Instead of the 13x9 baking dish, I used a shallow sheet pan with a non-stick rack (similar to a baking cooking rack). I put the skewered bacon wrapped water chestnuts on the rack and checked them after 15 minutes - not nearly done enough. This may be because we are at high altitude. I doubled the time and was satisfied with that. 

I dipped the partially cooked chestnut rollups into the sauce to coat them generously, then placed them back on the rack and they stayed in the oven for probably 45 minutes. You need to watch carefully at the end for the right amount of "lacquer" you want, because they can go from perfect to overdone in just a few minutes. Hands down, everyone loved them!

Gave 4 stars because I used other people's feedback and baked longer (25 minutes) before adding sauce. And cut the sauce to 1/4 and still had extra. With these two adjustments they turned out fabulous!

As always it was a huge success...my version is 4 cans of water chestnuts (drained of course). 2 pounds of bacon...sauce recipe as above (not doubled).
Cut bacon in half, wrap 1/2 around a whole chestnut and secure with the toothpick, place on a wire rack in a "half sheet cake pan" because they all fit. Bake for about 20 minutes without sauce to crisp up the bacon (plus or minus depending on your oven.) Drain the bacon fat...Put them and the rake back into the pan and baste the little goodies with the sauce...then I poured the rest of the sauce over them. Finish baking another 30 minutes or so (again, depends on your oven)...They were devoured!!! People ask for the recipe all the time...YUM!!!

These are VERY good. I no longer eat pork, so tried them with turkey bacon this time. They were still delicious, and much less greasy/fattening. I microwaved the turkey bacon in batches of 4 slices between 2 paper towels for around 30 seconds to get the cooking process started in the hopes they would crisp up faster, and that worked out great. I halved the slices and wrapped a whole water chestnut in each half. I cooked on a broiler pan, and just brushed the sauce on each wrap before baking for 30 minutes -- the turkey bacon cooks MUCH faster than pork bacon, as I recall having to cook the regular ones a lot longer.

The firest time I tried this recipe, I made them for a friend's birthday party, it was a huge hit! So many people raved about how wonderful they tasted. I doubled the batch and didn't have any left! I followed the recipe pretty closely, but I did add a few squirts of Sriracha Hot Chile Sauce to give it a bit of heat (just add to your taste). I only used half a strip of bacon to wrap the waterchestnut. I baked them longer until the bacon was crispy. Then I dipped them in the sauce and baked again for 10-15 longer so that the sauce was more of a glaze. I did not double the sauce, the amount of sauce was plenty, even though I doubled the amount of waterchestnuts/bacon I used. I also soaked the toothpicks in water so they didn't burn or turn dark brown. I served them in a crock pot set on low to keep them warm. Since then, I have received constant requests for me to make these again!

I looked all through the reviews on this recipe and made these few changes with amazing mouth watering results. Half all of the ingredients except the water chestnuts. Buy whole water chestnuts and cut them in halves. Cut the Bacon in half first vertically and then horizontally (the wrap will leave for great presentation). Use toothpicks! Preheat to 400 degrees while making the sauce. Wrap the bacon slices around the halved eater chestnuts and place toothpick into it to hold Bacon into place, do not add the sauce. Cook in 9x13 pan for 15 minutes at 400 degrees. Remove Bacon wrapped chestnuts and submerge them completely in the sauce. The more you put on the chestnuts the more of a "burnt" texture you receive, which is not a bad thing. Do not put the sauce in the pan, it softens the Bacon. Put the bacon wrapped sauce glazed chestnuts back into the oven for 15 additional minutes. Take out, cool for 10 minutes, and serve. You will not be disappointed.

These have been my faves for years. I do think they are better with only a third of a bacon slice per chestnut. Chestnuts are small and a half slice of bacon overpowers them. Other than that, I dont change anything. A keeper for sure!!
Everyone loved this. Will make it often.
My wife and I really enjoyed this. I added just a touch of hot sauce.

This will now be a must have for gatherings with friends. I just wished I'd read some of the suggestions ahead of time. I ended up broiling for a few minutes to get the crispiness of the bacon. Next time I will do what others before me suggested.

Slightly changed recipe! 1/3 strip of each thick-cut bacon, toothpicked to water chestnut that had been sprinkled with Worchestershire. Bake in oven 400 degrees til bacon is crispy (and fat rendered) about 30 min. Paint on BBQ sauce of your choice (I like Famous Dave's Devil's Spit), and continue in oven at 425 until the sauce has carmelized, another 15-30 min (watch oven).

I have made these aa few times they never disappoint.
This is a Christmas eve must have. It's become part of our family tradition to enjoy appetizers and drive around the city to see the beautiful lights.
I bake mine in a throw-away foil pan. So much easier than having to scrub a glass/ metal pan. You can also line your pan with non-stick foil.
